scope: SDK SIM direct [user_check] pointer forgery; no hardware, unbounded exploit, secret extraction or full-workflow claim

finding.primitive: host-supplied [user_check] pointers are dereferenced without an outside-enclave or range check; the host can name enclave-internal addresses for application reads and writes
finding.baseline: POSUP stores pathID over a .data word and reads a .data word pair; TrustFL reads 60,000 label bytes from image .text, writes 1,920,000 HMAC bytes into a mapped span, and reads a byte-verified 223,440-byte image prefix as training data (the fixed 47 MB loop then faults at the mapped-image boundary)
finding.protected: RADIX_ONLY/MAC27 abort in encbound_require/encbound_memcpy with ENCBOUND_ERR_POLICY (code=3) at the first raw enclave address

notes: POSUP targets a stable .data version-string word pair; the first .data word is the SDK g_is_first_ecall flag and is not used.

TrustFL label and training-data reads use image .text.  The fixed 47 MB training-data loop continues past the verified prefix and faults at the mapped-image boundary, so the child fault is isolated and every byte of the stable read-only prefix is checked.
TrustFL output targets the largest loaded read-write mapping inside the enclave extent (reserved memory); only BASELINE reaches the store.
limits: SDK SIM only; no SGX hardware.
No arbitrary-address sweep, secret extraction or code execution is claimed.
The host knows the enclave base and image layout in SIM, as a loader does; this is a demonstration premise, not a production address leak.
The read primitive returns HMACs of enclave memory, not the plaintext bytes; it is an equality/verification oracle with the known pre-init key.
